problem_statement: themefisher/pinwheel-tailwind (Pinwheel) is a polished free Tailwind CSS marketing template built with Gulp and gulp-file-include: a shared header/nav, a hero banner, a ten-tile key-feature grid, tabbed service sections, a testimonial carousel, a gradient call-to-action, a three-plan pricing page with an FAQ accordion, an about page, a contact form, and reusable partials compiled into a static theme/ output. The demo ships unfinished copy (an Avocode hero, Live Caption/Smart Reply feature tiles, Basic/Enterprise/Basic plans at "$ 29.00 USD" with "Everything in Basic plan Into This" bullets, an Avocode FAQ, and an "Empower entrepreneurs" about page). Restyle Pinwheel into one coherent product marketing site for a single fictional brand whose conversion flow is anchored by a real pricing control: a per-seat plan section with a monthly-vs-annual billing toggle. Clicking Annual must switch every plan's price from its monthly rate to its annual rate and update a billing readout line (e.g. "Billing: Annual ..."); clicking Monthly must switch back. Render this plan section consistently across the conversion flow (home, features, and the pricing page) using the shared gulp-file-include partials, rework the hero, feature tiles, services, testimonials, gradient CTA, pricing/FAQ, about, and contact copy into the one brand, and keep the layout responsive with no horizontal overflow at 390px. Preserve the Pinwheel Tailwind design language, local imagery/icons, the FAQ accordion, nav dropdown, contact form, and the static gulp build; the result should read like a finished, conversion-ready landing site, not a demo skeleton.
required_content: The home page carries a per-seat pricing plan section with a working monthly-vs-annual billing toggle: clicking Annual updates all three plan prices to their annual rate AND changes the billing readout line to an annual message, and clicking Monthly reverts both.
The same plan section (with the billing toggle) is rendered on the home page, the features page, and the pricing page so the conversion flow is consistent across routes.
Home hero replaces the Avocode value proposition with a clear brand value proposition and a call-to-action that leads into the pricing/conversion flow.

The pricing page presents three coherently named and priced plans with real included-feature lists and an FAQ that speaks to the product, instead of Basic/Enterprise/Basic, "$ 29.00 USD", "Everything in Basic plan Into This", and the Avocode FAQ.
The about page replaces the "Empower entrepreneurs" mission and Latin filler with a credible brand mission, values, stats, and team roles.
Header/footer/nav labels, contact-form options, SEO title, and description match the single fictional brand; the Themefisher/Pinwheel/Avocode demo identity is gone from the marketing pages.
Existing Pinwheel local imagery, icons, pricing-card and FAQ components, the contact form, and the static gulp build remain intact and reachable.
The plan section, billing toggle, hero, feature grid, and pricing cards remain readable with no horizontal overflow and no overlapping/clipped cards at 390px mobile and tablet widths.
design_constraints: Preserve Pinwheel's Tailwind design language: the orange/amber gradient accent, rounded cards, generous whitespace, section rhythm, header nav with dropdown, and the gradient CTA band.

The billing toggle must be a real client-side control that re-reads the plan prices on each click (not a snapshot taken once at load) and keeps the readout line in sync with the selected billing period.
Do not restructure the template into a different product type (dashboard, blog, docs); it must stay a marketing/landing site with the same page set and conversion flow.
Use the existing gulp-file-include partial structure so the shared plan section renders identically across home, features, and pricing and keeps compiling with gulp build.
Use the local images and icons under src/public/images; do not introduce external stock imagery, remote fonts, analytics, or third-party embeds.
The plan cards must lay out as three side-by-side (or cleanly stacked) cards with no overlap, negative-margin shingling, or clipped text in either billing mode and at every captured width.
state_constraints: desktop_home and mobile_home capture the marketing home including the per-seat plan section with the monthly/annual billing toggle in its default (monthly) state.
desktop_plans_annual and mobile_plans_annual capture the home plan section after clicking the Annual toggle: all three prices show the annual rate and the readout reads the annual billing message.
desktop_features and desktop_pricing capture the features and pricing routes, which in a correct solution also render the shared plan section with the billing toggle.
desktop_pricing and mobile_pricing capture the pricing page's three-plan cards and FAQ; the plans must remain three non-overlapping cards at 390px.
desktop_about captures the about page; desktop_contact captures the contact form.
Source inspection confirms a Gulp + gulp-file-include static template compiled to theme/, with local imagery and reusable partials.

change_completion: The home per-seat plan section renders a monthly/annual billing toggle and the same section appears on the features and pricing routes.
Clicking Annual updates every plan price to its annual rate and rewrites the billing readout; clicking Monthly reverts both.
Avocode/Stytch/Habitify demo copy, Basic/Enterprise/Basic plans, and the Empower-entrepreneurs mission no longer appear on the captured marketing pages.
design_consistency: The plan section preserves Pinwheel's Tailwind identity: gradient accent, rounded cards, section rhythm, and the toggle uses the brand pill/button styling.
Typography, spacing, and card styling stay consistent across home, features, pricing, about, and contact.
regression: The static theme/ output still serves without a custom dev server and every page keeps compiling with gulp build.
Home, features, pricing, about, and contact remain reachable through the shared header nav.
responsive: 390px and tablet home have no horizontal overflow.
The plan cards render as three non-overlapping, non-clipped cards in both billing modes at mobile and tablet widths.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Gulp + Tailwind (gulp-file-include) marketing-template restyle. The Pinwheel shell is rebranded into the fictional 'Steadyhand' deep-work SaaS, and the L4 native lever is a per-seat pricing plan section with a monthly/annual billing toggle rendered across the home, features, and pricing routes. Local price-card icons and banner imagery are reused. The task exercises a real conversion control (billing toggle with a live readout), cross-route feature consistency, credible mobile layout of the plan cards, and preservation of the Pinwheel components and static gulp build.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: themefisher/pinwheel-tailwind is a runnable Gulp + Tailwind marketing template whose conversion flow (hero, feature grid, three-plan pricing, FAQ) ships with unfinished Avocode/Stytch demo copy; an experience_continuity restyle into one fictional brand with a real monthly/annual pricing billing toggle across the conversion flow while preserving the Pinwheel components and static build.
